sampling_model.design: Finite semi-Markovian structural causal model with observed-context whole-row CSI constraints; identification is population-level and introduces no sampling randomness.
sampling_model.units: One population law on the fixed finite state space \(\prod_{i\in V}\mathcal X_i\).
sampling_model.treatment: The intervention is \(\operatorname{do}(X=\mathbf x)\), and the outcome cell is \(Y=\mathbf y\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every primitive CPT entry is strictly positive as an explicit technical scope condition; each derived divisor also carries its own positivity judgment.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Not part of the identification kernel; a returned observed-cell functional passes to downstream estimation.

Theorem 5 proves termination and soundness of CSI search, while Theorem 6 shows that separate identification in every context graph is not complete.

Theorem 1 is an if-and-only-if criterion for the labeled-DAG class with observed-root controls, treatment and outcome outside the controls, and maximal-regular labels; Algorithm 1 assembles the successful per-context formulas.
Theorem 1 proves soundness of a returned state-specific formula, and the paper does not claim general CSI completeness.
Theorem 1 characterizes classical positive-model identification through an invariant arithmetic-circuit cut found by the c-component method.

body.tldr: Fixed treatment and outcome assignments activate observed CSI information that variable-level identification can discard, but a local forest alone need not survive shared rows across contexts. In the settled fixed-nuisance binary-sink base case, the proved forest-to-kernel lift yields the verifier's canonical forest-supported rational null vector, and a positive baseline plus an explicit radius yields two global quotient-shared models with the same observed law and different queries. A new root-control bridge compiles maximal-regular observed-root labels into identical context graphs and row quotients and reproduces every successful published formula on the published class intersected with this note's fixed finite, strictly primitive-positive CPT class. The multi-block global dichotomy remains open and must be settled before any complete procedure is claimed.

project_justification.gap: Tikka et al. give sound CSI calculus and show that separate context graphs are incomplete. Mokhtarian et al. prove an if-and-only-if theorem for maximal-regular observed-root controls, but after intersection with this note's fixed-cardinality strictly primitive-positive CPT class only their successful identification formula transfers automatically. Chen and Darwiche give sound state-specific procedures without a complete obstruction theorem, and a local forest can be neutralized by cross-context row sharing.
project_justification.niche: Observed endogenous activation permits finite truth-table refinement while retaining shared CPT rows, reference-context recovery, cancellation, and information loss under active pruning.
project_justification.fill: The project certifies the exact binary-sink lift through a forest-restricted row-space alternative and baseline perturbation, proves an exact syntactic and successful-formula bridge for maximal-regular observed-root inputs, and leaves the provenance-carrying multi-block context-factor dichotomy visibly open.

body.related_work: Boutilier et al. define local CSI through equality of conditional behavior, and Pensar et al. encode such equalities by labels; these works inform the canonical quotient. Shpitser and Pearl establish ordinary formula-or-hedge completeness, recovered when the CSI list is empty. Tikka et al., Theorems 5--6, prove sound CSI search and show that separate context-graph identification is insufficient; the open global dichotomy would add necessity. Mokhtarian et al., Theorem 1, prove an if-and-only-if criterion for their labeled-DAG class under its maximal-regularity hypotheses, with control variables restricted to observed roots and treatment and outcome outside the controls. The root-control bridge proves identical compiled context graphs and row quotient and agreement of successful returned formulas. Because this note additionally fixes finite cardinalities and requires strictly positive primitive CPTs, the compiled class is the published class intersected with that stricter CPT class; only the published identification implication transfers automatically, not its nonidentification converse. Chen and Darwiche supply sound state-specific procedures and an active-pruning warning but no general completeness theorem. Their circuit work and Duarte et al.'s sharp polynomial programs inform finite algebraic contraction but do not provide a forest-derived shared-row kernel. Kivva et al. supply a positivity-aware generalized-identification comparator. Duarte and Solus characterize fully observed context-specific representations rather than latent query fibers. Bhattacharya et al. provide downstream estimation after a functional is returned, and the \(Y_0\) paper supplies the direct software consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: A rooted C-forest is not by itself a nonidentification certificate under shared CSI rows. In the reference-context bow, the \(A=0\) cells place the query coefficient in the observed row space and force structural rejection. Maximal active deletion also fails: in the five-node rational pair, the pruned graph has no hedge although the empty trace carries a kernel direction with query gap \(3/200\). The global theorem must therefore retain partial traces and prove a forest-supported kernel statement after all cross-context contractions; generic real-algebraic fiber testing does not supply this linkage or total arithmetic descent.
body.honest_scope: The canonical quotient, SUCCESS soundness, fixed-nuisance binary-sink affine map, forest-to-kernel row-space alternative, baseline perturbation soundness theorem, finite structural bound, two rational boundary fixtures, and root-control class bridge are supporting results. The bridge gives identical syntax and successful-formula agreement on maximal-regular observed-root inputs; it does not transfer the published nonidentification converse to this note's narrower fixed-cardinality positive intersection. The global context-factor dichotomy is visibly open and remains the completeness kernel. No general certificate-soundness or complete procedure is claimed before multi-block forest lifting is established. Strict primitive-CPT positivity and observed endogenous activation are transparent scope conditions. Estimation is downstream.
